paper_metadata.title: Refractory multi-principal element alloys MoxNbTiZry: Microstructure, mechanical properties and oxidation resistance
paper_metadata.journal: International Journal of Refractory Metals and Hard Materials

evidence.quote: Microstructures and properties of the MoxNbTiZry refractory multi-principal element alloys (RMPEAs) are investigated.

The Mo x NbTiZr y RMPEAs have excellent specific yield strength at high temperatures and relatively good ductility at room temperature
A phenomenological parameter δ Gb / γ is proposed to effectively estimate the room temperature ductility for Mo x NbTiZr y alloys and also other bcc solid solution RMPEAs.

The microstructures of MoxNbTiZry alloys are composed of bcc phases under different conditions, as shown by the XRD patterns in Fig. 1.
Both the arc-melted and heat-treated microstructures of Mo0.2NbTiZr alloy is composed of single-phase solid solution with homogeneously distributed compositions (Fig. 2a and b).

The arc-melted microstructure of Mo0.6NbTiZr alloy comprises of the (Mo, Nb)-rich region with light grey contrast and the Zr-rich region with dark grey contrast (Fig. 2c), in line with the broadening peaks in the XRD pattern compared with Mo0.2NbTiZr alloy (Fig. 1a and b).

The arc-melted microstructure of Mo0.6NbTiZr alloy comprises of the (Mo, Nb)-rich region with light grey contrast and the Zr-rich region with dark grey contrast (Fig. 2c), in line with the broadening peaks in the XRD pattern compared with Mo0.2NbTiZr alloy (Fig. 1a and b).

With further increase in Mo content, peak separation has obviously occurred for MoNbTiZr, indicating that two bcc phases have formed.
However, the peak separation is negligible for MoNbTiZr0.2 alloy with a higher Mo content and a considerably lower Zr content.
